evidence.finding: From 09:15 through 11:45, every reported service-level value is exactly 26 percentage points below answered_within_threshold / (offered_calls - short_abandoned_calls). At 11:45, for example, 60/63 = 95.24% versus 69.24% reported.
The displayed metric abruptly fell from a correctly calculated 81.33% at 09:00 to 48.42% at 09:15 and remained below the 80% target for the rest of the window.

Recalculated service level was below target at 09:15 (74.42%) and 09:45 (78.21%), but recovered to at least 85% from 10:00 onward; therefore the displayed sustained degradation was not operationally corroborated.

Several aggregate answered-call counts exceed the sum of queue-level answered calls by three, including 09:15 (81 versus 78) and 10:15 (86 versus 83), indicating an additional aggregation consistency issue.
During 09:15-11:45, offered demand totaled 864 calls versus 841 forecast, approximately 2.7% above forecast overall, with isolated higher intervals rather than a sustained surge.
Logged-in staffing remained fixed at 49, productive staffing stayed at 45-46, adherence remained 91.84%-93.88%, and no agents were in training.
No routing, platform, or other operational event was recorded to explain the exact and persistent 26-point reporting offset.

primary_root_cause_detail: Beginning at 09:15, the dashboard service-level field is systematically 26 percentage points below the value produced by the supplied metric definition. For example, 64 / (88 - 2) = 74.42%, not 48.42%; the same exact offset persists through 11:45. This reporting defect created the sustained below-target alert, although recalculated operational service level was mostly above target after the initial localized dips.
recommended_actions: Correct the dashboard service-level calculation or transformation that applies the 26-point downward offset, then backfill affected intervals from 09:15 onward.
Add automated validation that independently recalculates service level from component counts and alerts on any material mismatch.
Reconcile aggregate answered-call counts with queue-level totals and document whether backlog answers or aggregation logic account for the three-call differences.
Continue monitoring the isolated true service-level misses and use intraday load balancing if moderate volume increases concentrate in specific queues.

rejected_hypotheses.reason: Demand was only about 2.7% above forecast over the incident period and cannot explain an exact 26-point metric offset continuing through lower-volume intervals.
All 49 scheduled agents remained logged in, with 45-46 productive agents versus only 36-40 required.
Adherence remained stable between 91.84% and 93.88%, with no incident-aligned decline.
Actual AHT generally tracked forecast and did not rise persistently at incident onset.
No routing-change event was supplied, and queue patterns do not account for the uniform dashboard offset.
Some queues experienced episodic service variation, but staffing by queue remained constant and the variation cannot produce the exact aggregate reporting error.
Agents in training remained zero throughout the window.
No platform event or call-processing disruption was recorded.
Aggregate demand variance was modest and staffing exceeded forecast requirements throughout the window.

stakeholder_summary: CC-012 was a confirmed dashboard data-quality incident, not a sustained operational service failure. The reported service level was understated by exactly 26 percentage points from 09:15 through 11:45. Recalculation shows brief genuine misses early in the period but recovery to at least 85% from 10:00 onward. Staffing was stable and above forecast requirements; modestly elevated volume was contributory only.
